tasks.label: dbt docs: generate + serve (Warehouse)
tasks.detail: The one-click Demo 3 setup: generate the docs site against the Warehouse (~30 s, needs `az login`), then serve it on http://localhost:8080 and open a browser tab. Leave it running; the server keeps working even if the Azure token later expires.

tasks.label: dbt docs: generate (Warehouse)
tasks.detail: dbt docs generate --target warehouse, writing manifest.json + catalog.json + index.html into jaffle_shop/target. Queries the Warehouse for every column's type, so it needs `az login` and takes about 30 seconds. Same command the runbook uses; the task just dot-sources tools/env.ps1 first.
tasks.command: if (Test-Path './tools/env.ps1') { . './tools/env.ps1' } else { Write-Host 'tools/env.ps1 not found - copy tools/env.example.ps1 to tools/env.ps1 and fill it in.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }; & './.venv-warehouse/Scripts/dbt.exe' docs generate --target warehouse --project-dir jaffle_shop --profiles-dir jaffle_shop

tasks.label: dbt docs: serve on :8080
tasks.detail: Serve the docs already generated in jaffle_shop/target at http://localhost:8080 and open a browser tab. Serves files from disk: it still parses the project (so tools/env.ps1 is dot-sourced for the profile's environment variables) but never opens a connection, so it keeps working even after the `az login` token expires. Runs until you terminate the task.
tasks.command: if (-not (Test-Path './jaffle_shop/target/index.html')) { Write-Host 'No docs have been generated yet. Run the task "dbt docs: generate + serve (Warehouse)" instead.' -ForegroundColor Yellow; exit 1 }; if (Test-Path './tools/env.ps1') { . './tools/env.ps1' } else { Write-Host 'tools/env.ps1 not found - copy tools/env.example.ps1 to tools/env.ps1 and fill it in.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }; & './.venv-warehouse/Scripts/dbt.exe' docs serve --port 8080 --project-dir jaffle_shop --profiles-dir jaffle_shop

tasks.label: dbt docs: generate (choose engine)
tasks.detail: Same as the Warehouse task but for any of the three engines - each target uses its own virtual environment (.venv-warehouse / .venv-lakehouse / .venv-sqldb). Use it to show that the docs site is engine-specific: the compiled SQL and column types on each model page come from whichever engine generated them. The Lakehouse takes several minutes.
tasks.command: if (Test-Path './tools/env.ps1') { . './tools/env.ps1' } else { Write-Host 'tools/env.ps1 not found - copy tools/env.example.ps1 to tools/env.ps1 and fill it in.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }; & './.venv-${input:dbtEngine}/Scripts/dbt.exe' docs generate --target ${input:dbtEngine} --project-dir jaffle_shop --profiles-dir jaffle_shop

tasks.label: dbt docs: generate standalone HTML (demo fallback)
tasks.detail: Generate the docs as one self-contained file, jaffle_shop/target/static_index.html, and open it in the default browser. No web server and no connection to view it, so it is the safe fallback to prepare the evening before: if anything fails live, this file still has the full lineage graph. Generating it does need `az login`.
tasks.command: if (Test-Path './tools/env.ps1') { . './tools/env.ps1' } else { Write-Host 'tools/env.ps1 not found - copy tools/env.example.ps1 to tools/env.ps1 and fill it in.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }; & './.venv-warehouse/Scripts/dbt.exe' docs generate --static --target warehouse --project-dir jaffle_shop --profiles-dir jaffle_shop; if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { Start-Process './jaffle_shop/target/static_index.html' }

tasks.label: dbt docs: open the standalone HTML
tasks.detail: Open the already-generated jaffle_shop/target/static_index.html in the default browser. Nothing is regenerated, nothing is connected to - this works with no network at all.
tasks.command: if (Test-Path './jaffle_shop/target/static_index.html') { Start-Process './jaffle_shop/target/static_index.html' } else { Write-Host 'Not generated yet - run the task "dbt docs: generate standalone HTML (demo fallback)" first.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }

tasks.label: dbt: debug connection (choose engine)
tasks.detail: dbt debug against one engine: checks profiles.yml, the environment variables from tools/env.ps1, and opens a connection. The first thing to run if a docs generate or build fails - an expired `az login` shows up here in two seconds.
tasks.command: if (Test-Path './tools/env.ps1') { . './tools/env.ps1' } else { Write-Host 'tools/env.ps1 not found - copy tools/env.example.ps1 to tools/env.ps1 and fill it in.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }; & './.venv-${input:dbtEngine}/Scripts/dbt.exe' debug --target ${input:dbtEngine} --project-dir jaffle_shop --profiles-dir jaffle_shop

tasks.label: dbt build: everything (Warehouse)
tasks.detail: Demo 1. dbt build --target warehouse: 48 nodes (12 models + 33 data tests + 3 unit tests) in about 30 seconds. Seeds are disabled, so no raw data is reloaded. Expected tail: PASS=48 WARN=0 ERROR=0 SKIP=0. Afterwards open jaffle_shop/target/compiled/jaffle_shop/models/marts/customers.sql to show source() and ref() resolved to real table names.
tasks.command: if (Test-Path './tools/env.ps1') { . './tools/env.ps1' } else { Write-Host 'tools/env.ps1 not found - copy tools/env.example.ps1 to tools/env.ps1 and fill it in.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }; Write-Host 'dbt build --target warehouse' -ForegroundColor Cyan; Write-Host ''; & './.venv-warehouse/Scripts/dbt.exe' build --target warehouse --project-dir jaffle_shop --profiles-dir jaffle_shop

tasks.label: dbt build: choose engine + selection
tasks.detail: Any build against any of the three engines: pick the engine (each uses its own virtual environment) and how much of the DAG to build. Covers Demo 5 (everything on the SQL database) and any ad-hoc build. The Lakehouse is slow - a full build is ~7.5 minutes.
tasks.command: if (Test-Path './tools/env.ps1') { . './tools/env.ps1' } else { Write-Host 'tools/env.ps1 not found - copy tools/env.example.ps1 to tools/env.ps1 and fill it in.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }; Write-Host 'dbt build ${input:dbtSelection} --target ${input:dbtEngine}' -ForegroundColor Cyan; Write-Host ''; & './.venv-${input:dbtEngine}/Scripts/dbt.exe' build ${input:dbtSelection} --target ${input:dbtEngine} --project-dir jaffle_shop --profiles-dir jaffle_shop

tasks.label: dbt build: stg_orders+ (Demo 2, failure expected)
tasks.detail: Demo 2. Builds stg_orders and its 21 descendants on the Warehouse, then prints dbt's exit code in colour: green for 0, magenta for a failure. Broken (run the break task first): PASS=4 ERROR=1 SKIP=17 and exit code 1 - the reconciliation test fails on 61,465 orders and order_items/orders/customers are SKIPPED rather than built on bad numbers. Repaired: PASS=22, exit code 0. Because a failure is the expected outcome here, the task itself always exits 0 so VS Code does not flag it as broken on stage; the real code is the one printed on screen. The other build tasks do propagate their exit code, since a failure there is genuinely wrong.
tasks.command: if (Test-Path './tools/env.ps1') { . './tools/env.ps1' } else { Write-Host 'tools/env.ps1 not found - copy tools/env.example.ps1 to tools/env.ps1 and fill it in.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }; Write-Host 'dbt build --select stg_orders+ --target warehouse' -ForegroundColor Cyan; Write-Host ''; & './.venv-warehouse/Scripts/dbt.exe' build --select stg_orders+ --target warehouse --project-dir jaffle_shop --profiles-dir jaffle_shop; $code = $LASTEXITCODE; Write-Host ''; if ($code -eq 0) { Write-Host ('dbt exit code: ' + $code + '  -  green build, nothing downstream was skipped') -ForegroundColor Green } else { Write-Host ('dbt exit code: ' + $code + '  -  a test failed, so a pipeline or a pull request would stop right here') -ForegroundColor Magenta }; exit 0

tasks.label: dbt build: customers only (Lakehouse, ~2 min)
tasks.detail: Demo 4. dbt build --select customers --target lakehouse: the same model file, built on Spark by dbt-fabricspark over Livy. One mart plus its 4 tests, measured at 1 min 57 s. Warm the Livy session ten minutes beforehand (a cold session takes ~70 s to start) - runbook 'Before the talk' step 6.
tasks.command: if (Test-Path './tools/env.ps1') { . './tools/env.ps1' } else { Write-Host 'tools/env.ps1 not found - copy tools/env.example.ps1 to tools/env.ps1 and fill it in.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }; Write-Host 'dbt build --select customers --target lakehouse' -ForegroundColor Cyan; Write-Host ''; & './.venv-lakehouse/Scripts/dbt.exe' build --select customers --target lakehouse --project-dir jaffle_shop --profiles-dir jaffle_shop

tasks.label: dbt: list nodes (choose engine + selection)
tasks.detail: dbt ls: print the nodes a selection resolves to without building anything and without touching data. Instant, safe to run at any point, and the clearest way to show what the graph operators mean - `stg_orders+` returns stg_orders, order_items, orders, customers.
tasks.command: if (Test-Path './tools/env.ps1') { . './tools/env.ps1' } else { Write-Host 'tools/env.ps1 not found - copy tools/env.example.ps1 to tools/env.ps1 and fill it in.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }; Write-Host 'dbt ls ${input:dbtSelection} --target ${input:dbtEngine}' -ForegroundColor Cyan; Write-Host ''; & './.venv-${input:dbtEngine}/Scripts/dbt.exe' ls ${input:dbtSelection} --target ${input:dbtEngine} --project-dir jaffle_shop --profiles-dir jaffle_shop

tasks.label: Demo 2: break stg_orders (tax_paid left in cents)
tasks.detail: tools/scenario.ps1 break - edits one line of models/staging/stg_orders.sql so tax_paid is no longer converted from cents. Show `git diff` afterwards, then run the stg_orders+ build task and watch the test fail and the downstream models get skipped.

tasks.label: Demo 2: reset stg_orders from Git
tasks.detail: tools/scenario.ps1 reset - git checkout of models/staging/stg_orders.sql. It is code, so Git is the undo button. Always safe to run; `tools/scenario.ps1 status` says whether the model is currently broken.

tasks.label: Publish Lakehouse bundle (Spark runner)
tasks.detail: Publish the bundle NB_dbt_Runner_Spark runs (dbt project + dbt_packages, dbt-fabricspark, jaffle-dbt-runner + deps Runtime 2.0 lacks) to LH_Jaffle_Shop Files/dbt/jaffle_shop.zip in the chosen workspace. Runs from .venv-tools (tools\setup-env.ps1 -Target tools).

tasks.label: Publish Lakehouse bundle (Python runner)
tasks.detail: Publish the bundle NB_dbt_Runner runs (dbt project + dbt_packages, dbt-fabric + dbt-fabricspark + dbt-sqlserver, jaffle-dbt-runner + deps the Python-notebook image lacks) to LH_Jaffle_Shop Files/dbt/jaffle_shop_python.zip in the chosen workspace.

tasks.label: Assemble Lakehouse bundles (no upload)
tasks.detail: What CI does: resolve both bundles against their runtime manifests and build build/bundle-spark/jaffle_shop.zip and build/bundle-python/jaffle_shop_python.zip (+ deployment.json) locally, without authenticating or uploading.
tasks.command: ${workspaceFolder}/.venv-tools/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/publish_dbt_bundle.py --runner spark --assemble-only --out build/bundle-spark && ${workspaceFolder}/.venv-tools/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/publish_dbt_bundle.py --runner python --assemble-only --out build/bundle-python

tasks.label: Sync dbt project into Fabric dbt job items
tasks.detail: Copy jaffle_shop/ (minus seeds and profiles.yml, plus trimmed dbt_packages from dbt deps) into workspace/DBT_*.DataBuildToolJob/Code/dbt and point the items at it. Commit, push, then Source control -> Update in the workspace.

tasks.label: Tool and runner unit tests
tasks.detail: pytest over tools/tests and runner/tests (pytest.ini). No dbt or Fabric needed.

tasks.label: Refresh Fabric runtime constraints
tasks.detail: Regenerate tools/runtime_constraints/*.txt from Microsoft's runtime manifests: Spark Runtime 2.0 (conda YML) and the Python-notebook image, Python 3.11 kernel (newest release note). No-op until a manifest changes. Republish the bundles afterwards.

inputs.description: Fabric workspace name or GUID that contains LH_Jaffle_Shop
Which Fabric engine? Each uses its own virtual environment and profile target.
How much of the DAG? These are dbt's graph operators - + means 'and everything in that direction'.

options.label: stg_orders+  - stg_orders and all its descendants
--selector demo1  - the saved selector from selectors.yml
